source_organization: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology; PhysioNet (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center source data)
data_type: De-identified hospital and ICU electronic health record tables (diagnoses, medications, labs, events, timestamps). Credentialed access. Not open patient-level download without DUA.
usefulness_for_hetu: Longitudinal structured events can support research on temporal relationships, medication and diagnosis codes, and whether two documented facts could reasonably have been available to a clinician. Does not by itself label HETU root-cause categories.
access_requirements: PhysioNet credentialed user; CITI Data or Specimens Only Research (or equivalent as required by PhysioNet); signed PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement. Cloud/BigQuery access is requested separately after credentialing.
privacy_notes: De-identified under HIPAA Safe Harbor processes used by the MIMIC program; re-identification is prohibited. This is restricted clinical data, not public domain text to copy into fine-tuning files.
license_or_terms: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License 1.5.0 and PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0 (see the official project page).

source_organization: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology; PhysioNet
data_type: De-identified discharge summaries and radiology reports linkable to MIMIC-IV. Credentialed access.
usefulness_for_hetu: Free-text specialist and radiology documentation is the closest public research analog to specialist_a / specialist_b findings. Suitable for clinical NLP, terminology, and inconsistency research after authorization. Must not be copied into HETU training.jsonl.
access_requirements: Same PhysioNet credentialing, CITI training, and DUA as other MIMIC restricted projects; users must also have (or obtain) MIMIC-IV access as required by the project page.
privacy_notes: Notes are de-identified; still restricted. Do not redistribute notes or post them to GitHub.
license_or_terms: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License 1.5.0 and associated DUA (see official page).

source_organization: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology; Philips eICU Research Institute contributors; PhysioNet
data_type: Multi-center critical-care EHR tables (diagnoses, meds, labs, time-stamped events). Credentialed access.
usefulness_for_hetu: Multi-site ICU timelines support research on measurement variation, evolving impressions, and specialist documentation across units—relevant to no_fault versus gap distinctions at a research level.
access_requirements: PhysioNet credentialed user; required human-subjects / HIPAA training as stated on PhysioNet; signed credentialed DUA.
privacy_notes: De-identified multi-center ICU data; re-identification prohibited. Restricted, not a public note dump.
license_or_terms: PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data License 1.5.0 and PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement 1.5.0.

source_organization: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology; PhysioNet
data_type: Openly available subset of 100 patients with MIMIC-IV-like tables. Excludes free-text clinical notes.
usefulness_for_hetu: Useful to inspect schema, join keys, and event tables before requesting full MIMIC-IV. Not a substitute for notes-based contradiction labeling. Demo patients are still derived from real care and must not be treated as HETU synthetic fiction.
access_requirements: Open PhysioNet download for the demo project (see the official Files section). This is not a waiver of the DUA for the full credentialed MIMIC-IV database.
privacy_notes: De-identified subset; still real-derived EHR. Do not attempt re-identification. Demo is public metadata/schema practice, not a license to copy records into SFT JSONL.
license_or_terms: See the official PhysioNet demo project page for the posted license of the demo files (distinct from full MIMIC-IV credentialed terms).

dataset_name: National NLP Clinical Challenges (n2c2) research data sets
source_organization: Harvard Medical School Department of Biomedical Informatics (continuing former i2b2 NLP shared tasks)
data_type: Fully de-identified clinical notes and shared-task annotations (medications, concepts, relations, longitudinal records depending on year). Individual registration.
usefulness_for_hetu: Established clinical NLP benchmarks for medications, concepts, and longitudinal notes. Useful for evaluating extractors that might later feed HETU-style contradiction detection. Challenge labels are not HETU root-cause labels.
access_requirements: Each user must register, access independently through the DBMI Data Portal, and honor the n2c2 Data Use Agreement. Files must not be shared with others or posted to GitHub.
privacy_notes: De-identified notes remain restricted by DUA. Do not redistribute.
license_or_terms: n2c2 Data Use Agreement (academic and corporate previews linked from https://n2c2.dbmi.hms.harvard.edu/data-use-agreement).
